Duryodhana goes home and tells his uncle Shakuni he would rather die than live with this. Shakuni tells him there is no need for either.
The new assembly hall
An invitation to dice
Dhritarashtra builds a new assembly hall and invites Yudhishthira to a friendly game of dice. Vidura carries the invitation, and his face says what his words cannot.
Yudhishthira accepts. A king does not refuse a challenge.
Warn Yudhishthira that Shakuni's dice cannot lose
He thanks you, and takes your hand, and goes anyway. "If I am called, I must play," he says.
Go to the hall
Stay away. You want no part of it
You stayed away from the dice game.
The assembly hall, Hastinapura
The first throws
The stakes
Shakuni throws for Duryodhana. Yudhishthira stakes his jewels and loses. Then his gold, his chariots, his servants, his army and his kingdom. Every throw goes the same way.
Then he stakes his brothers, one by one, and loses them. Then he stakes himself, and loses.
Bhishma, Drona and Kripa sit very still. Dhritarashtra keeps asking who has won.
You are standing among the courtiers by the pillars.
Call out that Shakuni's dice are false
You have watched Shakuni's hands, and you say exactly what they are doing. Shakuni smiles. Nobody stops the game, but Vidura looks at you as if marking your face for later.
You shout, and the hall turns to look at you. Shakuni asks, very kindly, whether you would like to inspect the dice yourself. People laugh.
Beg Bhishma to stop the game
Bhishma looks at his hands. "The way of dharma is subtle," he says, and says nothing more.
Stay silent. It is the king's game
Leave the hall now
You walked out of the dice game before the worst of it.
The question no one answers
Draupadi's question
Yudhishthira stakes Draupadi, and loses her. Duryodhana sends for her as a slave. She sends back a question: did he lose me before or after he lost himself?
Dushasana drags her into the hall by her hair. She stands before the elders and asks again. No one answers her.
Then Vikarna, one of Duryodhana's own brothers, stands up: a man who has lost himself has nothing left to stake. The hall shouts him down.
Stand beside Vikarna and answer her question out loud
You spoke against him in the hall.
In the dice hall you answered Draupadi's question out loud. Dushasana marked you.
The Pandavas will trust you. Dushasana will not forget
Step between Dushasana and Draupadi
You held Dushasana's wrist in the dice hall, for one breath, before the guards pulled you off.
You catch Dushasana's wrist and hold it for one long breath before the guards drag you back. The hall saw it.
Dushasana's guards throw you to the floor before you reach him. You taste blood on the marble.
Beg Duryodhana, as his oldest friend, to stop this
You begged him to stop, in front of everyone.
He looks at you as if he has never seen you before.
Say nothing
You were in the hall, and you said nothing.
Leave the hall. You cannot watch this
The cloth that does not end
Karna, who has not forgotten the swayamvara, says she is a slave now and may be treated like one. Duryodhana bares his thigh to her.
Dushasana takes hold of her garment and pulls. It does not end. However hard he pulls, there is more cloth, until he falls back exhausted on a heap of it.
Bhima rises and swears, before everyone, that he will break Duryodhana's thigh and drink Dushasana's blood on the battlefield.
Outside, jackals are howling in daylight. The old king is afraid.
Swear your own vow that this will be answered
You already hold three vows.
Tell Karna he is better than this
You told him he was better than what he said in the hall.
Karna does not look at you. His jaw is tight. Later you will wonder whether he agreed.
Remember every face in the hall, and what each one did
You memorised every face in the dice hall: who spoke, who laughed, who looked away.
Look at the floor until it is over
Frightened by the omens, Dhritarashtra offers Draupadi boons. She asks only for her husbands' freedom, and their weapons.
Then Yudhishthira is called back for one more game. The loser will go into exile for twelve years, and a thirteenth year in hiding. He loses.
The road out of Hastinapura
The Pandavas walk into exile
Thirteen years
The Pandavas walk out of Hastinapura in deerskins, with Draupadi beside them, her hair still unbound. Kunti stays behind with Vidura.
The city watches in silence. Everyone knows that when the thirteen years end, there will be war.
Follow the Pandavas into the forest
You followed the Pandavas into exile.
Stay at Hastinapura and watch Duryodhana rule
You stayed at the Kuru court through the exile years.
Go home, make your fortune and raise a family
You went home to make your own life.
As a warrior. The world he will grow up in needs them
You raised Vasu to be a warrior.
To be kind before he is brave
You raised Vasu to be kind before he was brave.
In your own craft, so he can earn a living without a sword
You taught Vasu your own craft.
An ashram on the upper Ganga
A hermitage in the mountains
A season at the ashram

Arjuna has gone north alone to seek divine weapons from the gods. The rest of the camp moves between hermitages. You spend a season at an ashram where the sages will teach anyone patient enough to sit still.
Practise penance and ask for a divine weapon
After a season of penance you were granted a divine weapon.
On the last night of the season, a voice in the fire gives you a mantra. You will be able to call an astra once in any battle. You will also be responsible for where it lands.
No weapon comes. But you leave the ashram quieter and clearer than you arrived.
Learn from the ashram's healers
The ashram's healers taught you their remedies.
Serve the sages: carry water, sweep, keep silent
The sages do not know you yet.
An old sage blessed you with foresight.
On the last day, the oldest sage touches your forehead. "You were kind to one of us once, on a dusty road," he says. You never told anyone.
Hunt for the camp, which is always hungry
The Kamyaka forest
An empty hermitage
Jayadratha
While the Pandavas are out hunting, King Jayadratha of Sindhu, Duryodhana's brother-in-law, finds Draupadi alone at the hermitage and carries her off in his chariot.
You are the first to hear her shout. Jayadratha's guards are covering his escape.
Go after the chariot
Run to find Bhima and Arjuna
You find them by the river and point the way. Bhima is already running before you finish.
Guard Dhaumya and the hermitage in case they come back

The Pandavas catch Jayadratha. Bhima shaves his head in five tufts as a mark of shame, and Yudhishthira lets him go. Jayadratha goes straight into the mountains to pray for a boon: one day on which he can hold back every Pandava except Arjuna.
After Jayadratha's chariot
Sindhu guards on the forest road
Two of Jayadratha's guards turn their horses to block the path.
Sindhu guard
Sindhu archer
You cut through Jayadratha's rearguard when he carried Draupadi off.
The guards break. Ahead, you can hear Bhima roaring.
They leave you in the dust. Bhima runs past you without stopping.
A lake in the forest
A still lake in the heat
The lake of questions

In the twelfth year, the brothers grow desperate with thirst. One by one, Nakula, Sahadeva, Arjuna and Bhima go to a lake, ignore a voice that tells them to answer its questions first, drink, and fall down as if dead.
Yudhishthira comes last, and agrees to answer.
You came with Bhima. Your own throat is cracked with thirst, and the water is right there.
Drink. You cannot think for thirst
Darkness, and then you are lying on the bank in the evening, alive, with a strange heaviness in your limbs that never quite leaves.
Wait, and listen to the questions
At the lake you heard the questions. What is faster than the wind? The mind. What is the greatest wonder? That every day people die, and the living act as if they never will.

What is faster than the wind? The mind. What is more numerous than the grass? Thoughts. What is the greatest wonder? That every day people die, and the living act as if they never will. You remember every answer for the rest of your life.
Pleased with Yudhishthira's answers, the voice gives back his brothers' lives. It was Dharma himself, testing his son.
The edge of the Dvaita forest
Royal tents near the forest
The cattle count

Duryodhana takes his court to the forest, saying it is to count the royal herds. Everyone knows it is to show off in front of the exiled Pandavas. A band of Gandharvas, forest warriors who serve no king, ambushes the royal camp. Karna's line breaks.
Duryodhana is being dragged off in chains.
Fight the Gandharvas
Run to the Pandavas' camp for help
Yudhishthira hears you out and sends Arjuna and Bhima at once. "He is still our cousin," he says.
Get out with the rest of the court

Arjuna and Bhima free Duryodhana on Yudhishthira's orders. Rescued by his enemies, Duryodhana tries to starve himself to death from shame. His friends talk him out of it, and he comes home hating the Pandavas more than ever.
The Gandharva ambush
Forest warriors in the royal camp
Gandharva warrior
You hold your corner of the camp, but Duryodhana has already been carried off.
They knock you down and leave you. At least you stayed.
The river at dawn
Karna at his morning prayers
Karna's armour

Karna was born with armour and earrings that make him almost impossible to kill. Every morning after his prayers to the sun, he gives anyone whatever they ask. One morning an old brahmin asks for the armour. Everyone says it is Indra, Arjuna's father, in disguise.
Push through and warn Karna it is a trick
You tried to save his armour.
"I know who he is," Karna says quietly. "I gave my word to give what is asked." He cuts the armour from his own body, and the brahmin gives him a spear in return that can kill anyone, once.
Watch in silence
Ask {teacher} to teach you the weapon you were promised
Your teacher must think you have earned it.
{teacher} taught you to call a divine weapon.
{teacher} looks at you for a long time, then teaches you the mantra in a whisper. "Never against someone who cannot fight back," he says.
A life of your own
Trade along the rivers
Open a healer's house
Teach the village children to fight
Take your field back from Sudatta's men
Sudatta's men
A fence across your family's field
A hired club-man
Sudatta's men leave and do not come back. The village brings sweets.
They keep the field. You keep your pride, more or less.
The fever year
A fever comes up the river in the dry season. Half the village is sick, the granary is low, and the nearest king is busy with his own troubles.
Tend the sick yourself
You nursed your village through the fever year.
You lose eleven people. Without you it would have been many more.
You do everything you can. The fever takes its own count.
Ride to the next kingdom and come back with grain
Go into the forest to find Mauni, your old teacher
Mauni gave you medicine for the village, and a divine weapon for what was coming.
Mauni is older, and just as silent. He gives you a bundle of roots for the fever, and then, before you leave, a mantra. "You kept my secret," he says. "Keep this one too."
King Virata's court, Matsya
The lake country of Matsya
The hidden year

For the thirteenth year the Pandavas must live unrecognised. They take service at King Virata's court: Yudhishthira as a dice master, Bhima as a cook, Arjuna as Brihannala, a teacher of dance, Draupadi as a queen's maid.
When the king's commander Kichaka will not leave Draupadi alone, Bhima kills him one night in the dancing hall.
With Kichaka dead, the Kauravas raid Matsya's cattle. Young Prince Uttara rides out to stop them, with the dance teacher Brihannala as his charioteer.
Ride out with Prince Uttara to save the herds
Ride with the Kaurava raiders
Recognise Brihannala, and keep the secret
You recognised Arjuna in Matsya and kept his secret.
You know that walk, even in bangles. When your eyes meet, Arjuna puts a finger to his lips. You say nothing to anyone.
Brihannala is just a dance teacher to you. Later you will feel a fool.
Brihannala is Arjuna. He takes up his bow Gandiva, defeats the whole Kaurava force alone and drives them home. The thirteen years are over. Arjuna's son Abhimanyu marries Virata's daughter Uttara.
The cattle raid on Matsya
Dust over the grazing grounds
Kaurava horseman
Kaurava archer
You fought beside Prince Uttara when the Kauravas raided Matsya.
The raiders on your flank turn back. Ahead, one chariot is driving the whole Kaurava army before it.
You are unhorsed. From the ground you watch one chariot drive the whole Kaurava army before it.
Raiding Matsya's herds
A lone chariot comes for you
Matsya's cowherds fight harder than anyone expected. Then the arrows start coming from a single chariot.
Matsya cowherd
Brihannala's chariot
Somehow you hold. Around you the rest of the army is running.
At Matsya you were routed, with the whole Kaurava army, by a single chariot.
Like everyone else, you wake up in the grass, unhurt and stripped of your upper cloth, while the chariot drives away with the herds.
The river at dusk
The river where a basket once floated
The secret of Karna's birth

Krishna meets Karna before the war and tells him the truth: he is Kunti's firstborn son, born before her marriage, set adrift on the river. He is the eldest Pandava. If he changes sides, he will be king.
Karna refuses. Duryodhana stood by him when no one else would, and he will not leave him now.
Tell Karna you have always known, and that it changes nothing for you
You knew who he was all along, and stayed his friend.
Karna laughs, for the first time in weeks. "Then you are the only one in the world who has not changed their mind about me today."
Urge him to take the crown and stop the war
"And be remembered as the man who betrayed his only friend for a throne?" he says. "No."
Tell him you will stand with him, whatever he decides
Kunti comes to Karna at the river and asks him herself. He promises her she will still have five sons when the war ends: he will kill no Pandava except Arjuna.
Thirteen years, gone
Not a needle's point
The Pandavas ask for their kingdom back. When that is refused, they ask for five villages. Krishna goes to Hastinapura himself to plead for peace.
Duryodhana says he will not give them as much land as the point of a needle can cover. Both sides gather their armies at Kurukshetra.
Fight for the Pandavas
Fight for the Kuru throne under Duryodhana
Refuse to fight. Serve in the healers' tents, which take in both sides
You refused to fight, and went to serve in the healers' tents.
Kurukshetra, before the first day
Two armies facing each other
Before the first arrow
Eighteen armies face each other across the plain of Kurukshetra. Conch shells sound from both sides.

Arjuna drives his chariot out between the two armies and looks at his teachers, his grandfather and his cousins on the other side. He puts down his bow. Krishna, his charioteer, speaks to him for a long time.
You are too far away to hear the words. You only see Arjuna stand up at last and take up his bow again.
In the front line, with your weapon
Driving a chariot for a warrior who needs one
You need some skill with a chariot.
Commanding a company
You need a strategist's training or a commander's presence.
In the healers' tents
Singing to the troops before every battle
Your tent, the night before
A lamp in a tent
Vasu asks to ride with you
Keep him beside you, where you can see him
Order him to stay in the camp
He argues, then sulks, then obeys. The camp is behind the lines. It should be safe.
Let him join another company. He has to learn without you
Kurukshetra · days 1 to 9
Bhishma commands the Kaurava host
Nine days of Bhishma
For nine days Bhishma, the grandsire, commands the Kaurava army, and no one can stand against him. He has promised not to kill the Pandava brothers themselves. He kills nearly everyone else.
Fight in the line
Guard the supply lines and the river crossings
Work in the healers' tents through the nine days
In the first nine days of the war you saved more lives than you could count.
You stop counting the ones you save. You never stop counting the ones you lose.
There are too many of them, and too few of you.
You fall back with the broken line. No one blames you. You blame yourself.
You let a wounded enemy crawl away. Someone else will kill him, or no one will.
You fell at Kurukshetra.
Days one to nine
You survived the first nine days of the war.
When the conches sound at sunset, you are still standing.
You fell in the first days of the war, when Bhishma was still unstoppable.
Kurukshetra · day 10
A bed of arrows at dusk
The bed of arrows
On the tenth day the Pandavas put Shikhandi at the front of Arjuna's chariot. Bhishma will not fight one who was born a woman, and lowers his bow. Arjuna's arrows bring the grandsire down.
He falls on a bed of arrows, so many that his body does not touch the ground. He has the boon of choosing the hour of his death, and he chooses to wait.
That night, warriors from both armies lay down their weapons and come to see him.
Ask him how a person can know their duty
On the bed of arrows, Bhishma told you that duty is subtle, and that keeping your word can still lead you into wrong.
"With difficulty," he says, and almost smiles. "I kept my word all my life, and look where it has brought us."
Ask him about the vows you have made
"A vow is a promise to the person you will become," he says. "Be careful what you promise them."
Bring him water
He thanks you, but he does not drink. Later Arjuna shoots an arrow into the earth, and a spring of clear water rises to the old man's lips.
Stay away. You cannot face him
Kurukshetra · days 11 and 12
Drona takes command
Take the king alive

Drona takes command of the Kaurava army. Duryodhana wants one thing from him: capture Yudhishthira alive, so the war can be won with another game of dice. For two days Arjuna stays close to his brother, and the plan fails.
Guard Yudhishthira's chariot
Drive for Yudhishthira's chariot
Carry the wounded off the field under fire
You carried the wounded off the field on the eleventh and twelfth days.
Seven trips into the dust and back. Seven people who will see their families again.
On the fourth trip a horse goes down on top of you.
Guarding the king
You fall back, and others close the gap you left.
You let the last of them go.
Around Yudhishthira's chariot
You guarded Yudhishthira's chariot when Drona tried to take him alive.
The attack breaks against your line. Yudhishthira raises a hand to you as his chariot turns.
You fell guarding Yudhishthira's chariot on the eleventh day.
Kaurava chariot-warrior
The drive for the king
You pull back with the rest of the attack.
You let a wounded guard crawl back to his lines.
Yudhishthira's guard
You break through the guard, just in time to see Arjuna's chariot arrive and end the attack.
You fell trying to take Yudhishthira alive on the twelfth day.
Pandava guard
Kurukshetra · day 13
The wheel formation
Drive into the breach after Abhimanyu
There may be no way back
Hold at the gate and try to force it open
Pull back to get Vasu out when the line breaks
On the thirteenth day you pulled back to save your son.
Hold your place in the ring as ordered
You were part of the ring that closed on the boy.
On the thirteenth day you held your place in the ring that closed on Abhimanyu.
Refuse to close in on a lone boy
You lowered your bow and would not close in.
On the thirteenth day you lowered your bow and would not close in on Abhimanyu.
Leave the ring to carry a wounded boy out
Work the tents behind the wheel

Abhimanyu fights until his bow is broken, then with his sword, then with a chariot wheel. Many warriors surround him at once, and he falls. That night Arjuna swears to kill Jayadratha before the next sunset, or walk into fire.
Into the wheel
Through the breach
You are through the breach before it closes.
You fell in the breach of the Chakravyuha, trying to follow Abhimanyu.
Holding the gate
You pull back from the gate.
The breach Jayadratha holds
The gate never opens. But you held your ground in front of it.
You were among those who could not break through.
On the thirteenth day you were among those who could not break through.
Whatever you do, Jayadratha's line does not break today. Nothing would have broken it.
You fell at the breach of the Chakravyuha, trying to reach Abhimanyu.
Jayadratha's guard
Inside the Chakravyuha
The gap closing behind you
Inside the wheel
Stay beside Abhimanyu to the end
You fell beside Abhimanyu in the heart of the wheel, on the thirteenth day.
Cut your way back out while you still can
You turn the chariot and drive at the weakest part of the wall. You come out the other side bleeding, alone, and alive.
Kurukshetra · day 14
A sun that seems to set early
Sunset and torches

All day Arjuna cuts his way toward Jayadratha, who is hidden deep behind the Kaurava lines. Near evening the sky darkens as if the sun has set. Jayadratha steps out to watch Arjuna fail. The sun is still up, and Arjuna's arrow finds him.

The fighting does not stop at dusk. For the first time, the armies fight on by torchlight. To save the Pandavas from Karna, Bhima's son Ghatotkacha fights through the dark until Karna is forced to spend the one spear that could have killed Arjuna.
Clear the road for Arjuna's chariot
Guard the ground in front of Jayadratha
Fight on in the night battle
Carry torches for the healers searching the field
You find a boy from your own country under a dead horse, and drag him out alive.
The road to Jayadratha
You fall back from the road.
You let him go.
Day fourteen
You break a hole in the line, and Arjuna's chariot goes through it like water.
You fell on the fourteenth day, clearing the road for Arjuna.
Guarding Jayadratha
You fall back toward Jayadratha's hiding place.
You hold your ground all afternoon. It does not matter. The sun is still up.
You fell on the fourteenth day, guarding Jayadratha.
Pandava chariot-warrior
Pandava footsoldier
The night battle
You fall back into the dark.
You let him go into the dark.
Torchlight on the field
You survived the night battle of the fourteenth day.
Dawn comes. You are still alive, and you cannot remember most of the night.
You fell in the dark on the night of the fourteenth day.
Kurukshetra · day 15
An elephant named Ashwatthama
Ashwatthama is dead
Drona cannot be beaten while he holds his bow. Bhima kills an elephant named Ashwatthama, the same name as Drona's son, and shouts that Ashwatthama is dead.

Drona does not believe it. He asks Yudhishthira, who has never told a lie. Yudhishthira says, "Ashwatthama is dead," and then, under his breath, "the elephant." Drona lays down his weapons, and Dhrishtadyumna kills him where he sits.
Shout it along the line: Ashwatthama is dead
Refuse to repeat it
Ride to Drona and tell him his son is alive
You reach his chariot and shout it. He looks past you, toward Yudhishthira, the one man he trusts not to lie. He does not hear you.
Stay with the wounded
When it is over, Ashwatthama hears how his father died. He swears by everything he knows that the Pandavas will pay.
Kurukshetra · day 16
Karna takes command
Bhima's vow
Karna takes command of the Kaurava army. On the sixteenth day, Bhima finds Dushasana on the field and fulfils the terrible vow he made in the dice hall, thirteen years ago.
Fight Dushasana's men
Dushasana's men
You escape them in the press of the battle.
Day sixteen
On the sixteenth day Dushasana sent his men for you, and you survived them.
His men lie in the dust. Across the field, Bhima has found Dushasana.
On the sixteenth day, Dushasana's men found you. He had not forgotten the dice hall.
Dushasana's bodyguard
The sixteenth day
You fall back.
You survive another day.
You fell on the sixteenth day.
Kurukshetra · day 17
A chariot wheel sinks into the earth

Arjuna and Karna meet at last. In the middle of the duel, Karna's chariot wheel sinks into the earth, as a brahmin once cursed it would. He reaches for the mantra of his greatest weapon, and it is gone from his mind, as his teacher Parashurama once cursed it would be.
He climbs down to lift the wheel and asks Arjuna to wait, as the rules of war demand.
Loose an arrow at Karna while he lifts the wheel
On the seventeenth day you shot at Karna while he was lifting his chariot wheel.
Shout to Arjuna to wait until Karna is armed
You called out for a fair fight.
Jump down and help Karna lift the wheel
The wheel moves. It moves too slowly.
The earth will not give it back.
Stand over Karna and fight to the end
You fell beside Karna on the seventeenth day, standing over him as the wheel sank.
You will not survive this
Pull back while you can. Vasu is waiting
Watch, and remember
Kurukshetra · day 18
The last day
Shalya leads what is left of the Kaurava army and falls to Yudhishthira. Sahadeva kills Shakuni, who started all of this with a pair of dice.

Duryodhana, alone, hides in a lake. The Pandavas find him and he comes out to fight Bhima with the mace. Bhima strikes him on the thigh, below the waist, against every rule of mace fighting. Balarama, who taught them both, has to be held back from striking Bhima.
It is the last day. Survival is not certain.
Fight in the last battle
Go to the lake to witness the duel
The last battle
You fall back, for the last time.
You let him go. The war is nearly over.
Day eighteen
You survived the eighteenth and last day of the war.
There is no one left to fight.
You fell on the eighteenth day, the last day of the war.
The lakeside at dusk
A broken king by the water
Duryodhana at the lake
Duryodhana lies where Bhima left him, his thigh shattered. He is waiting to die. He sees you, and for a moment he looks like the boy at the lotus pond.
Sit with him, and talk about when you were young
You sat with him at the end.
You sat with Duryodhana by the lake as he lay dying.
Tell him what he did to all of you
"I lived as a king," he says. "I am dying as one. Which of them can say that?"
Leave him to the night
Before midnight, Ashwatthama comes to the lake. Duryodhana makes him commander of an army of three: Ashwatthama, Kripa and Kritavarma.
The Pandava camp, the night after the last day
Fire in the sleeping camp
The night raid
The war is over. The Pandava camp sleeps for the first time in eighteen days. Ashwatthama, mad with grief for his father, comes through the gate in the dark with a sword.
Run to Vasu's tent
On the night of the raid you got Vasu out of the burning camp.
You drag him out under the back of the tent, into the dark, and you do not stop running until the fire is a glow behind you.
Wake the camp
On the night of the raid your shouting woke enough of the camp to save many lives.
Your voice carries. Tents empty into the dark. Many who should have died that night live.
The smoke takes your voice. Too few hear you.
Fight Ashwatthama at the gate
Go with Ashwatthama into the sleeping camp
You went into the sleeping Pandava camp with Ashwatthama.
Refuse him
"Then go home," he says, "and live with that."
Try to stop him
Ashwatthama at the gate
You run, like everyone else.
Fire in the camp
You fought Ashwatthama at the gate of the burning camp, and lived.
He breaks away from you and vanishes into the smoke. You held him for long enough that some got out.
You died at the gate of the Pandava camp, fighting Ashwatthama in the dark.
Standing in Ashwatthama's way
The road to the sleeping camp
You tried to stop Ashwatthama on the road to the sleeping camp.
He staggers, and then goes around you. You cannot stop him. You slowed him down.
You died on the road, trying to stop Ashwatthama from reaching the sleeping camp.
Kurukshetra, after
Dawn over the field
The women on the field

The women of both houses come to the battlefield to find their dead. Gandhari, who has worn a blindfold all her married life so as not to see more than her husband could, walks among her hundred sons.
In her grief she curses Krishna: as the Kuru clan destroyed itself, so will his own Yadavas, thirty-six years from now. Krishna accepts the curse without a word.
At the water rites, Kunti tells her sons that Karna was their eldest brother. Yudhishthira weeps for a long time.
Help build the pyres for the dead of both sides
Sit with your own dead and let no one move you
Swear vengeance on Ashwatthama
He has been cursed to wander the earth. You could follow
The grandsire's last teaching
The last teaching
Bhishma has waited on his bed of arrows for the sun to turn north. Before he dies, he teaches Yudhishthira how to rule, at great length, while the Pandavas and the survivors listen.
You sit at the edge of the crowd. When he pauses, he looks at you as if he expects a question.

The Kuru heartland, on the upper Ganga

A city of palaces, granaries and old dynasties on the banks of the Ganga, ruled by the blind king Dhritarashtra on behalf of the Kuru line. The princes, Pandavas and Kauravas alike, grow up within its walls.
Born here, you stand closest to every great event of the epic: the tournament, the dice game, the councils of war. Loyalty to the throne comes easily. Standing apart from it does not.
Between the Ganga and the Yamuna, south of the Kurus
A rich and learned kingdom of archers, scholars and fire-priests, with its capital at Kampilya. King Drupada's court values what you can do over who your father was.

Drona will train the Kuru princes to take Drupada prisoner, so a child of Panchala begins with a grudge on one side and a welcome on the other. Draupadi, born from Drupada's sacrificial fire, will one day be your princess.
West of the Yamuna, a land of lakes and pastures
A small, gentle kingdom of cattle herders, horse breeders and lake fishers, ruled by King Virata from his capital at Viratanagara.
Greater powers rarely look this way, which is why the Pandavas will choose it for their year in hiding. Children here grow up among horses, and many become fine charioteers.
The western coast, at the edge of the sea
A walled island city of the Yadava clans, built on the sea for safety. Its harbours bring traders, sailors and envoys from distant lands.
The Yadavas are kin to both sides of the coming war. Born here, you learn diplomacy early, and you will see your own clan divided when the armies gather.
The far east of the Ganga plain, on the Champa river
A prosperous eastern kingdom of rice fields, river ports and elephant forests, with its capital at Champa.
Duryodhana gives Anga to Karna, the charioteer's son, to make him a king. Its people love Karna for it, and here a person is judged more by deeds than by birth.
The charioteers' quarter at the edge of Hastinapura
The sutas drive the chariots, tend the horses and sing the deeds of kings. They stand beside every great warrior in battle, yet the nobles never treat them as equals.
You grow up in the same lane as Adhiratha, who found a baby floating in a basket and raised him as Karna. Doors will close because of your birth, and you will learn to open them anyway.
The forests between the river and the hills
Hunters, fishers and forest guides who live outside the cities' order and the rules of caste. They know every path, plant and animal of the deep forest.
Ekalavya, the Nishada prince who taught himself archery, comes from people like yours. The cities look down on you, but in the forest no prince can match you.
The far northwest, beyond the Indus
A mountain kingdom on the great trade roads, where many peoples, languages and gods meet. Queen Gandhari and her brother Shakuni came from here to Hastinapura.
At the Kuru court you will always be a foreigner. Shakuni will take you for one of his own, and others will wonder whose side you are really on.
